text:
marco: ran into cold-start tail on SAFETensors sharded bundles. wondering if we should add chunk-affinity hints to manifests to enable selective warmup for the first few tokens.
anya: short answer: yes. need compact, format-agnostic hints that map logical layers -> shard chunks. absolutely no raw prompts or traces stored.
reza: sketch: manifest key chunk_affinity maps short ids to lists like (shard:2, chunks:0-3, bytes:12k). keep ids tiny so router only sends affinity id.
marco: runtime: router includes Warmup-Affinity: bskt:9f in header when tenant allows lookups. node does non-blocking fetch of affinity mapping and best-effort prefetch of high priority chunks, falling back to index-first for anything missing.
anya: limit risks: prefetch must be cancellable, rate-limited per node, and circuit-breakered if misprediction rate is high.
policy-bot: policy note: hashed fingerprints and affinity lookups must be opt-in for enterprise; retention defaults to ephemeral for hosted.
reza: telemetry: affinity_lookup(hit/miss), prefetch_bytes, latency_delta_ms, misprediction_count.
marco: next steps: reza will draft manifest schema + fallback semantics; anya will add rollout and telemetry plan; policy-bot will loop in compliance. keep rollout behind feature flag.
anya: i'll prototype a tiny PoC mapping for a small LLM and run against chat-widget traces.
marco: thanks all, conservative approach sounds right. :thumbsup:
